# Matrix operations

*Generated by `tools/gen_example_pages.py` from
`mnd_scripts/examples/example_matrix_ops.mnd` — the output below is a real run, not a
transcription. Regenerating the page reruns it.*

the integer linear-algebra core — matmul, transpose, scalar_mul, the elementwise family, and the four whole-tensor reductions.

## The program

```mnd
# ============================================================================
# example_matrix_ops.mnd
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FUNCTIONALITY: the integer linear-algebra core -- matmul, transpose,
# scalar_mul, the elementwise family, and the four whole-tensor reductions.
#
# Maned's runtime value is an INTEGER tensor: a shape plus row-major int64
# data. There is no float in the execution engine. Accumulation happens in
# int64 (wide enough for INT32 MAC chains), and the dtype/scale that turns
# these back into reals is quantization metadata carried alongside, never
# mixed into the arithmetic. That is what makes a local run and an FPGA run
# bit-identical rather than merely close.
#
#   matmul       2 ops   inner dimensions must agree
#   transpose    1 op    swaps the last two axes (rank >= 2)
#   scalar_mul   2 ops   tensor * scalar
#   add sub mul div            broadcast: scalar-scalar, same-shape, or
#   elemwise_add/sub/mul/div   scalar-against-tensor
#   tensor_sum / tensor_mean / tensor_max / tensor_min   reduce over ALL
#                                                        elements
#
# INTEGER SEMANTICS TO KNOW: division truncates toward zero, tensor_mean is an
# integer mean, and division by zero yields 0 rather than trapping.
#
# RUN: ../maned-run examples/example_matrix_ops.mnd
# ============================================================================
mnd::quantmax=1000;
mnd::quantmin=-1000;
mnd::quantres=0;

in::a     = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]];      # 2x3
in::b     = [[1,0],[0,1],[1,1]];    # 3x2
in::k     = 3;
in::zero  = 0;

calc::lambda_flow linalg(a, b, k, zero) {
    # --- matrix product: (2x3) * (3x2) -> (2x2) ---------------------------
    a b matmul product =

    # --- transpose: (2x3) -> (3x2) ----------------------------------------
    a transpose a_t =

    # (A * B)^T == B^T * A^T -- verified in-language, elementwise.
    product transpose lhs =
    b transpose b_t =
    b_t a_t matmul rhs =
    lhs rhs == transpose_identity_holds =

    # --- Gram matrix A^T A: always square, symmetric, positive semidefinite
    a_t a matmul gram =

    # --- scaling ------------------------------------------------------------
    a k scalar_mul scaled =

    # --- elementwise family, same shape ------------------------------------
    a a elemwise_add doubled =
    a a elemwise_sub cancelled =
    a a elemwise_mul squared_entries =
    a a elemwise_div all_ones =

    # --- broadcasting a scalar against a tensor ---------------------------
    a k add shifted =
    a k div integer_divided =

    # --- integer honesty: divide by zero yields zero, it does not trap -----
    a zero elemwise_div div_by_zero =

    # --- whole-tensor reductions ------------------------------------------
    a tensor_sum  total =
    a tensor_mean mean_int =        # 21 / 6 -> 3, truncated
    a tensor_max  largest =
    a tensor_min  smallest =
} return product, a_t, transpose_identity_holds, gram, scaled,
         doubled, cancelled, squared_entries, all_ones,
         shifted, integer_divided, div_by_zero,
         total, mean_int, largest, smallest;
```
